newsitem.title: ITALY: FOCUS-ENI shares slip as Italy ups placing.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-ENI shares slip as Italy ups placing.

text.p: Shares in Italy's energy giant ENI slid on Friday after the Italian Treasury increased the size of its second tranche share offer, already one of Europe's biggest placements this year, due to strong demand from investors.

The Treasury said late on Thursday it would offer 1.1 billion shares in the state-controlled oil and chemicals group, rather than the original tender of 700 million shares, pushing the stake on sale to 13.75 percent from 8.75 percent.
ENI shares slipped due to concern over more shares coming onto the market and were 2.36 percent lower at 7,130 lire by midsession in a generally lower Milan stock market.

The offer of shares to the Italian public has been running all this week and closes on Friday with the price of the shares being announced on Saturday, October 26, and trading in the new shares set to start on Monday, October 28.

Analysts said that the Treasury needed to be cautious at the start of the offer as it was uncertain about demand for the shares and market conditions at that time. But strong demand had encouraged it to increase the placement.
It was not clear who would be offered the extra 400 million shares but analysts said the majority was likely to be offered to private rather than institutional investors.

A Treasury statement late on Thursday said it had been advised by coordinators of the placing, Italian investment bank IMI and CS First Boston, that "demand for the shares from the Italian public and institutional investors, already strong in the first place, had been increased further".
The Treasury had earlier said demand was double the amount on offer to the public after only three days of the public offer.

The original scheme announced earlier this month for the 700 million shares included a 300 million share offer to Italian retail investors, 235 million to institutional investors and 165 million to investors in the United States.

In addition, there was an over-allotment, or "green shoe", option for a further 105 million shares to be offered to institutions if demand was heavy. The Treasury now says the green shoe could be up to 15 percent of the 1.1 billion share issue.

Last weekend, the Treasury said that retail investors would get a 3.5 percent price discount to the closing price on Friday October 25 and it set the maximum price they would pay at 7,425 lire. Analysts expect that institutions will be offered a one to two percent discount to the October 25 closing price.
Ironically, the fall in the ENI share price is likely to mean slightly less money for the Treasury in an issue which is set to raise almost eight trillion lire ($5.2 billion).
The ENI offering is the largest share placement in Europe this year, although it will soon be overtaken by the partial privatisation of Deutsche Telekom in November.

The first tranche of ENI shares was floated on the Milan, London and New York markets in November 1995. The 15 percent stake sold at 5,250 lire a share and raised 6.3 trillion lire for the Treasury. ($1=1,527 lire)
